instruction: When all requested experiment work and result verification are complete, commit and push the results to the remote repository.
finish_checks: Reconcile every registered case, seed, budget, conditional skip, interruption and retry with immutable original records.
Investigate unresolved required cases and preserve explicit limitations if additional authorized attempts cannot obtain solutions.
Independently validate all reported solutions and separate proven optimality gaps from feasible-reference differences and lower-bound certificates.
Verify frozen source/input hashes and absence of unresolved reference conflicts.
Report single-call and cumulative rerun time, feasibility coverage, proof counts and failed/resource-limited runs.
deliverables: Final report, case coverage, run tables, GAP/time efficiency tables and relevant plots.
Experiment plan, environment/version metadata and evidence of the rental-cost override.
Checksummed archives of frozen portable sources, inputs, cases, solutions, independent audits, trajectories and original logs, split into repository-compatible parts where necessary.
Reproduction/restoration instructions and the IO-recovery incident record.
Task-owned portable runner/adapter changes and relevant tests.
git_handling: Inspect current local changes and remote updates before preparing the delivery commit.
Preserve unrelated pre-existing local work and use an isolated checkout if that avoids mixing changes.
Do not force-add local AGENTS.md, runtime launchers, machine-specific documentation, virtual environments, licences or secrets.
Preserve raw hashed artifact bytes through appropriate Git attributes.
Do not force-push; retain any newer remote commits.
Verify the final commit exists on origin/main and report its hash and remote link.
Delete the follow-up automation only after experiment completion and successful delivery, or report any actual remaining blocker.
